record.context_brief: Gaussian simplex partitions and noise stability
record.original_question: Fix 0 <= rho <= 1. Among all partitions of R^n into q parts of equal Gaussian measure, where 3 <= q <= n+1, is the maximum noise stability at rho achieved by a standard simplex partition, and for -1 <= rho <= 0 does the standard simplex partition minimize the noise stability?

evidence.quote: Statement: Fix 0 <= rho <= 1. Then among all partitions of R^n into 3 <= q <= n + 1 parts of equal Gaussian measure, the maximal noise stability at rho occurs for a standard simplex partition. Further, for -1 <= rho <= 0 the standard simplex partition minimizes noise stability at rho.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let n ≥ 2 and 3 ≤ q ≤ n+1 be integers. Equip ℝⁿ with the standard Gaussian probability measure γₙ (density (2π)^{-n/2} exp(-|x|²/2)). For ρ ∈ [-1,1], the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck noise operator acts on f ∈ L²(ℝⁿ, γₙ) by
  T_ρ f(x) = E[f(ρx + √(1-ρ²) Z)],
where Z ~ N(0, Iₙ) is independent. Given a measurable partition A = (A₁, …, A_q) of ℝⁿ with γₙ(Aᵢ) = 1/q for every i, define its noise stability at parameter ρ by
  S_ρ(A) = ∑_{i=1}^{q} ∫_{ℝⁿ} 1_{Aᵢ}(x) · T_ρ 1_{Aᵢ}(x) dγₙ(x).
A "standard simplex partition" of ℝⁿ is one obtained as follows: fix q unit vectors v₁, …, v_q ∈ ℝⁿ that form the vertices of a regular (q−1)-simplex centered at the origin (so ⟨vᵢ, vⱼ⟩ = -1/(q−1) for i ≠ j), and set
  Aᵢ = {x ∈ ℝⁿ : ⟨x, vᵢ⟩ = max_{1 ≤ j ≤ q} ⟨x, vⱼ⟩},  i = 1, …, q.

Prove or disprove the following two assertions:

(a) For every ρ ∈ [0, 1], the maximum of S_ρ(A) over all measurable partitions of ℝⁿ into q parts each of Gaussian measure 1/q is attained by a standard simplex partition.

(b) For every ρ ∈ [-1, 0], the minimum of S_ρ(A) over the same class of partitions is attained by a standard simplex partition.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (often called the Standard Simplex Conjecture of Isaksson–Mossel) is largely open in the equal-measure regime. Heilman established a partial result for q = 3, n ≥ 2 and 0 < ρ < ρ₀(3,n). Heilman–Mossel–Nazarov showed that standard simplex partitions are NOT the most noise-stable partitions when the prescribed measures are unequal (and that plurality is not the most stable low-influence discrete partition in those cases), but the equal-measure case treated here is not refuted by their work and remains open in general.

status_evidence.title: Euclidean Partitions Optimizing Noise Stability (Heilman)
status_evidence.snippet: Proves the Standard Simplex Conjecture for k=3, n≥2 and 0<ρ<ρ₀(k,n).
status_evidence.claim: Partial proof in the case q=3 for small positive ρ.

status_evidence.title: Standard Simplices and Pluralities are Not the Most Noise Stable
status_evidence.snippet: Standard simplex is not the most stable partition for unequal prescribed measures; the equal-measure conjecture is not refuted.
status_evidence.claim: Disproves the conjecture in the unequal-measure setting; the equal-measure version remains open.

status_evidence.title: Maximally Stable Gaussian Partitions with Discrete Applications (Isaksson–Mossel)
status_evidence.snippet: Original formulation of the Standard Simplex Conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Origin of the conjecture under consideration.
